subject: Operational metrics & SLO verification — procurement checklist
messages:
From: Alyssa Green <alyssa@clearwave.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@clearwave.com>
Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLO measurement details for procurement

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement needs a short packet on how Redwood measures uptime and latency for the hosted inference API before we can move to contract review. They asked for:

- Short definition of the SLOs (what "uptime" and latency percentiles mean for Redwood)
- Monitoring stack and where metrics are recorded
- Alerting thresholds and escalation path (who gets paged)
- What customers can see (dashboards, raw telemetry, sampling rate)
- Temporary exception or carveout process (how to request, approval timelines)

Can you send something concise we can include in our vendor questionnaire? Procurement is on a short timeline — ideally by EOD Friday.

Best,
Alyssa
Head of Vendor Ops
ClearWave Analytics
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Green <alyssa@clearwave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO measurement details for procurement

Thanks Alyssa — happy to summarize. Below is the short packet; attaching a zip with supporting screenshots and a one-page runbook. If you need anything added for your legal/procurement team let me know.

---START SUMMARY---
1) SLO definitions (hosted API)
  - Uptime: percent of 1-minute evaluation windows in which control-plane+data-plane request success rate >= 99.5%. Success = 2xx or 3xx responses; excludes scheduled maintenance windows pre-notified in SLA.
  - Latency: p95 and p99 of end-to-end server-side token generation latency measured on the service side (excluding client network). For procurement we publish p95 and p99 for 1-minute rolling windows.

2) Monitoring stack
  - Metrics emitted by runtime -> Prometheus at aggregation targets -> long-term storage in Cortex (retention 90 days default).
  - Traces captured via OpenTelemetry, sampled at 10% by default (configurable per-customer with contract).
  - Alerting rules live in Alertmanager; we back these with on-call rotations in PagerDuty.

3) Alerting thresholds & escalation
  - Infra-critical (e.g., control-plane 5m error rate spike > 2%) -> P1 page to SRE on-call (PagerDuty) + Slack #sre-incidents channel.
  - Latency degradation (p95 increase > baseline + 30% sustained 5m) -> P1 alert, SRE triage within 15 minutes.
  - Persistent or degraded customer-observed errors -> Engagement of CS/Account team within 1 business hour.

4) Customer visibility
  - We provide a read-only Grafana dashboard per account showing uptime, p95/p99 latency, error-rate, and request rate.
  - Customers may request a one-time export of raw telemetry (CSV) for a bounded time window; exports are sampled to preserve cost (default sampling 1:10 for token-level logs).
  - Customers on Dedicated or Private deployments can opt into higher fidelity traces and longer retention per negotiated terms.

5) Exception / carveout process
  - Short-term exceptions (e.g., temporary sampling reduction, additional retention) can be requested by your Security/Compliance or Procurement contact.
  - Requests submitted via the vendor questionnaire or support portal -> reviewed by Product/SRE within 3 business days -> may require additional controls (NDA, IP access, support fees).

---END SUMMARY---

Attachments: slo-evidence-bundle.zip (screenshots + runbook) and a text file with a one-click Grafana invite link.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Eng. — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 22 May 2025 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: procurement follow-up and exception limits

Ben / Karthik — quick notes before I send to Alyssa:

- Procurement will often push for raw request-level logs. We should state the default sampling and also a clear cost/controls ladder: e.g., full request logs only under Dedicated/Private or with a commercial add-on + SOC2 attestation we've received.
- For trace retention beyond 90 days, require an addendum. We should offer a standard SLA carveout template (1 page) that explains timelines: approval typically 2-3 weeks if legal review needed.
- Karthik: can you confirm the exact on-call paging thresholds and the canonical PagerDuty escalation policy name so I can include it in the packet?

I'll also include language about "reducing sampling for customers wanting ad hoc exports" instead of promising full exports.

—Marissa
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 May 2025 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: procurement follow-up and exception limits

Marissa / Ben — confirmed items for the packet:

- PagerDuty escalation policy: "Runtime-NOC -> Senior-NOC -> Oncall-Eng-Lead". P1 paging: immediate; P2 notifications to email/Slack. I recommend calling out the 15 minute initial ack SLA for P1.
- Default trace sampling: 10% with per-customer opt-in to 100% for Dedicated/Private under contract.
- Export process: one-off raw telemetry exports are supported but require a signed data request and may be rate-limited; typical turnaround 3-5 business days.

If procurement pushes on retention/exports, route them to me and Marissa and we'll prepare the addendum template.

Karthik
SRE Manager — Redwood Inference

Alyssa — sending the packet we discussed and a short checklist you can paste into your questionnaire.

Checklist for procurement (copy/paste):
- Uptime definition: 1-minute windows, success >= 99.5% (excl. notified maintenance).
- Latency: server-side p95/p99, published as 1-minute rolling aggregates.
- Monitoring: Prometheus + Cortex (90d retention), traces via OpenTelemetry (default 10% sample).
- Alerts: P1 ack SLA 15 minutes, PagerDuty escalation policy "Runtime-NOC -> Senior-NOC -> Oncall-Eng-Lead".
- Customer access: read-only Grafana dashboards; ad-hoc raw exports via signed request (may be sampled).
- Exception path: submit an exception request; Product/SRE review within 3 business days, legal review may add 2 weeks.

Attached: slo-evidence-bundle.zip (contains screenshots of Grafana, sample alert rules, and an exception-request template). Grafana invite link included in the zip and also as a standalone text file: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSLOEvidence

Let me know if procurement wants any of the exact alert rule YAML or the PagerDuty escalation ID — happy to provide.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Solutions Eng.
Redwood Inference
